venue.cap_derivation: AGENTS.md 6.1 formula at this session's live home: host `available` was 22 GiB, so cap = min(8 GiB, 22 - 16) = 6 GiB, with OPENSSL_RS_COURT_MEMSWAP equal to it; the 2 GiB floor was met. Host headroom above the container cap is therefore >= 16 GiB, which is the property the 24 GiB pre-build floor exists to protect.
venue.build_floor_deviation: DISCLOSED DEVIATION: AGENTS.md 6.1 rule 2 says `available < 24 GiB -> do not start a build`. Host `available` was 22-23 GiB throughout (44 GiB of 45.8 GiB swap already in use), so the literal floor was NOT met. The batch proceeded only on the explicit instruction of the orchestrator, which recreated the court with the formula-derived 6 GiB cap and accepted the >= 16 GiB host headroom above the cap as the protected property. This is a deliberate, recorded exception, not a claim that the floor was satisfied.

does_not_prove: Single host, self-connection: client and server are the same 0.0.49 build on loopback. A failure could not be localised to one side, and agreement between them is not evidence of interoperability with any other implementation.
No third-party peer: no upstream, BoringSSL, rustls or commercial SSH implementation was used other than the authority-linked OpenSSH reused for w5.

Functional evidence only (AGENTS.md section 8): no ASan/valgrind/Miri run, no adversarial or fuzzing court (section 13), no constant-time or timing measurement (section 11), no Wycheproof/ACVP vectors in this batch.
This is a functional L7 replay only. It does not re-measure the safety closure, does not re-adjudicate any mechanism, and says nothing about the 301 carried-forward P1000 families.
L7 functional PASS is not SAFE_COMPATIBLE graduation (section 7): it says nothing about the safety obligations of the mechanisms these binaries reach.
Authentication policy is deliberately permissive for the probe (PermitRootLogin yes, StrictModes no, root login with pubkey). This exercises the crypto path, not a hardened baseline.
Concurrency is 16 simultaneous loopback logins, not sustained load and not a rekey-under-load workload.
The executed session binary is the stripped install copy 881591410052, not the link-tree binary 771e8734766d. Same install provenance; byte-equivalence is not proven.
The matrix is not exhaustive: it covers the algorithms the Phase-17 probe names plus default negotiation, not every kex/cipher/MAC/host-key combination the build advertises.
The authority differential covers key-file compatibility for RSA/ECDSA/Ed25519 and legacy PEM in both directions; it does not cover certificates, PKCS#8, DSA, or signature verification policy.

The authority-linked OpenSSH and the candidate share the same OpenSSH 9.9p1 source and version text; only the resolved libcrypto differs. The differential tests two OpenSSL implementations behind one OpenSSH version, not two OpenSSH releases.

The batch ran under a 6 GiB court cap derived from the AGENTS.md 6.1 formula, below the literal 24 GiB pre-build floor (disclosed deviation, see venue.build_floor_deviation). Peak container memory.current stayed under 1 GiB for every command and the cgroup recorded no OOM event, but the floor's own margin was not available and this batch is therefore not evidence that the floor is unnecessary.

No census and no closure receipt bind this install to the source tree in this batch. The source link is asserted from the pinned install digests, the empty `git diff v0.0.49 -- src Cargo.toml Cargo.lock build.rs`, and a read-only recomputation of src_content_sha256; it is not a census of the installed artefacts.
residuals: keyformat-049.sh reports 0 NOT_RUN and 0 FAIL: AUTH_KG points at auth-b85, so every authority read executed; w5 is an independent second differential.

The authority tree auth-b85 was REUSED, not rebuilt: its ssh-keygen resolves the pinned authority prefix libcrypto (611e511db427..., 7295816 B) and the prefix digest equals the pin. No auth-049 tree exists, and byte-equivalence to a fresh authority build is not claimed.

The four scripts are generated by court/freeze-049/l7/derive_049.py from the b85 originals with exact whole-line replacements; derivation.diff is the complete delta and contains only header/paths/ports.
The court was recreated for this batch (cap 6 GiB, 8 CPU), so /court scratch was reset; the derived scripts and all captures live in the bind-mounted /work and were unaffected.
court/ is git-ignored, so these scripts and transcripts are invisible to git status and must be added with `git add -f` if the orchestrator wants them tracked.
The executed sshd-session and sftp-server are the stripped install copies; the evidence binds the executed digests and the tree digests separately rather than asserting they are the same bytes.
OpenSSH 9.9p1 omits finite-field DH from its default kex list; the probe re-enables group14/16/18 and gex explicitly, so those cases are not default 9.9p1 negotiation.
The Phase-17 'EXPECT FAIL' labels for ECDSA/RSA host keys are stale: both pass. The labels are left verbatim to keep the case set byte-identical, and the actual result is recorded here.

src_content_sha256 has two defensible rules in this repository: the supplied value 557f7190... is over every file under src/ (885 files), while the historical census tool hashes *.rs only and yields ade50c7383cf... (878 files, the value court/freeze-b86/census-b86.json records for source_head 53141c4b). Both are recorded; neither is presented as the other.

The first attempt at this replay stopped before any build because host `available` was 23 GiB < the 24 GiB floor; that refusal is recorded in court/freeze-049/l7/BLOCKED.md. This run proceeded only under the orchestrator's explicit disclosed deviation, with the formula-derived 6 GiB cap.

OPENSSL_RS_COURT_MEM and OPENSSL_RS_COURT_MEMSWAP are honoured only by `up`; every cap figure in this file was read from the live cgroup via `bash docker/openssl-rs-court.sh status`, not inferred from the requested values.

A zombie sshd-session (pid 16988, state Z, no exe link) remained after the supplement run; it is the deferred child of the supplement's sshd and cannot be reaped inside the container. The supplement script already selects a live session by testing `-r $p/exe`, so the zombie cannot be mistaken for the executed session, and the identity witness in the transcript was taken from the live process while it ran.
scope_statement: This file records observed L7 functional behaviour of the 0.0.49 OpenSSH consumer binaries on one host against themselves and against an authority-linked OpenSSH key-format peer. It does not certify memory safety, cryptographic assurance, interoperability, or SAFE_COMPATIBLE graduation, and it does not re-measure the safety closure or adjudicate any mechanism.
